claims.text: HfNbTiVAl10 has an as-reported hierarchical heterostructure with multilevel chemical fluctuations.
High-resolution microstructural imaging can quantify chemical fluctuations and phase connectivity in this heterostructure.
A machine-learning model can be calibrated using a limited set of high-fidelity tensile and fracture tests.
Controlled furnace cooling below 600 °C, rather than rapid quenching, produces the reported hierarchical state.
Prior studies have validated a compositional range within which the proposed model can be used.
Spatial chemical-fluctuation metrics and interphase-connectivity indices mediate the relationship between processing, microstructure, and mechanical performance.
The proposed microstructural descriptors capture the essential heterostructural features that influence mechanical behavior.
Machine learning can correlate microstructural descriptors with measured tensile and fracture responses to predict mechanical properties.
The hybrid approach can bypass extensive CALPHAD and density-functional calculations.
Ab initio and molecular-dynamics calculations are time-consuming, and CALPHAD can require significant computing resources.
Existing computational approaches have not adequately explored complex relationships among descriptors and thermomechanical properties to accelerate alloy design.
Existing methods are less effective for predicting fracture toughness.
The hybrid method will improve prediction accuracy by roughly 20% relative to conventional methods.
The hybrid method will double computational efficiency relative to conventional methods.
The hybrid method will reliably predict Young's modulus, yield strength, and fracture toughness for hierarchical HfNbTiVAl10.
The model may become unreliable for processing-induced microstructures that differ substantially from its training data.
Extreme rapid cooling or altered phase distributions may place the material outside the model's reliable domain.
The model may fail if its descriptors omit emergent features in modified compositions.
Extrapolation to alloys with substantial compositional drift is uncertain because machine-learning performance depends on the composition of the training set.
The hypothesis is falsified if blinded predictions exceed approximately 20% relative error or if descriptor-property correlations are not statistically significant.
